chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The waiting period (iddah) of mut'ah (temporary marriage) is forty-five days, and for precaution (ihtiyat) it is forty-five nights.'

key_terms.الِاحْتِيَاطُ: Precaution (ihtiyat), often used in fiqh to denote a safer or more cautious calculation
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period (iddah) for a woman after divorce or death of husband

ai.seo_question: What is the duration of the waiting period (iddah) for temporary marriage (mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the iddah for temporary marriage (mut'ah) as forty-five days, while highlighting a jurisprudential precaution (ihtiyat) of counting forty-five nights to ensure the period is fully completed. This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly approach to reconciling textual evidence with practical legal certainty, ensuring the woman's status is clearly defined before she may remarry.
